chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Husayn ibn Ahmad al-Minqari, from Isa al-Zarir who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): A man kills a man deliberately — what is his repentance? He said: He should make himself available (to the guardians of the slain). I said: He fears they will kill him. He said: Then let him give them the blood money (diya). I said: He fears they will come to know (it was him) because of that. He said: Then let him be mindful of the blood money and make it into small packages, then watch for the times of the prayers and place them in their home.

key_terms.الدِّيَة: Diya — blood money paid in compensation for a killing; a fixed sum in Islamic law that may substitute for retaliation (qisas)
key_terms.تَوْبَة: Tawba — repentance; here used in the jurisprudential sense of making amends for a criminal act, not merely spiritual contrition
key_terms.صُرَر: Surar — small bundled packages; the method of secret delivery to avoid identification
key_terms.مَوَاقِيتَ الصَّلَوَاتِ: Mawaqit al-Salawat — the times of the prescribed prayers; chosen because the victim's family would be at the mosque, making secret delivery possible
key_terms.مُتَعَمِّداً: Mutaammidan — deliberately/intentionally; the legal category of premeditated homicide, which triggers qisas

ai.seo_question: What is the repentance for deliberate murder according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: This hadith presents a dialogue between Isa al-Zarir and Imam al-Sadiq (AS) about the repentance of a deliberate killer. The Imam provides a graduated path: first, self-surrender to the victim's family for retaliation (qisas); if that is feared, payment of the blood money (diya); and if even that risks exposure, delivering the diya secretly in small packages at prayer times when people are away from their homes. This ruling reflects the Shia jurisprudential hierarchy that prioritizes the rights of the victim's family, while offering a practical path toward making amends even in circumstances of fear.
